description: Desarrollamos un Rover todo terreno con cámara integrada y seguidor solar giratorio (servomotor, panel solar y fotorreceptor) para optimizar la carga energética. Incorpora sensor ultrasónico para detección de obstáculos, medición de temperatura, humedad y presión atmosférica, y telemetría por radiofrecuencia (2.4 GHz) hacia una estación terrena con pantalla OLED, ideal para explorar sitios terrestres análogos a la Luna y Marte sin depender de internet.
summary: BAO Rover Explorer is a modular space robotics prototype by Byron Ortega for the Building Junior challenge. It combines an Arduino planetary rover with a 2.4 GHz wireless Ground Control Base (real-time OLED radar, buzzer, and LED alerts) and an interactive web simulator modeled on NASA Goddard DONKI space weather advisories to protect missions from collisions and solar radiation.
details:
How it works:

BAO Rover Explorer is a wireless planetary rover prototype. It uses an Arduino UNO, ultrasonic radar (HC-SR04), climate sensor (DHT11), and solar panel to detect obstacles under 35 cm. It sends live telemetry via 2.4 GHz RF to a Ground Control Base (OLED screen, buzzer, LED alerts) and an interactive web drive simulator.

Benefits & Impact:

It helps overcome space communication delays by demonstrating autonomous obstacle avoidance and solar power monitoring. It also serves as a scalable testbed to train future aerospace engineers.

Tools & Hardware:

Arduino UNO, HC-SR04, DHT11, 2.4 GHz RF modules, OLED display, solar panel, C++ (Arduino IDE), HTML/CSS/JS, and official NASA Goddard (DONKI) space weather records.

Creativity & Factors:

It creatively combines real physical telemetry with a hands-on web simulator (forward, auto-brake, reverse). We prioritized 2.4 GHz link stability, instant collision alerts, and future scalability to a 6-wheel Rocker-Bogie rover with LiDAR.
